uncited: Domain-Specific Adaptations modify the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework to handle non-RGB, non-photometric data such as medical volumes, microscopy stacks, and ultrasound probe intersections [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md], [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md], [5170-ultragauss-rendering.md].

While standard 3DGS optimizes for novel-view synthesis of RGB scenes using calibrated camera poses and photometric losses, these adaptations replace the projection target with volumetric supervision, voxel-space rasterization, or 3D geometric intersections [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md], [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md], [5170-ultragauss-rendering.md].
Loss functions include L1, MSE, Dice, or Tversky, applied to voxel grids or sampled points [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md], [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md].

**Voxel-Space Rasterization/Sampling:** Rendering involves sampling the Gaussian field at voxel centers or within a voxel grid, often using trilinear interpolation of the volume data to supervise the Gaussians, rather than projecting Gaussians onto a 2D image plane [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md].

**Initialization from Volume:** Initial Gaussian positions are seeded directly from the input volume data (e.g., gradient-weighted samples, uniform grid, or ROI mask sampling) rather than from Structure-from-Motion (SfM) points [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md], [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md].
**Normalization:** Input volumes are normalized to $[0, 1]$ to stabilize optimization, often with dataset-specific outlier clipping [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md].
Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced for novel-view synthesis of RGB scenes [1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].

AVIS and Microscopy adaptations address the need for compact, interactive visualization of large 3D/4D scientific datasets (medical CT/MR, fluorescence microscopy) where voxel grids are too large and ray-marching is too slow [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md], [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md].
UltraGauss addresses the specific physics of ultrasound, where data is acquired as intersecting planes rather than projected views [5170-ultragauss-rendering.md].
